record.original_question: Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces carrying the nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics that arise from dynamic free boundaries or vortex sheets in hydrodynamics.

evidence.quote: Problem 36. Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces equipped with such H −1/2 -metrics obtained as metrics on dynamic boundaries or vortex sheets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote a shape space of smooth closed hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (for instance, the space $\mathrm{Emb}(M,\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of unparametrized embeddings of a closed manifold $M$), and consider on $\mathcal{S}$ the family of nonlocal Riemannian metrics of fractional Sobolev order $H^{-1/2}$ that arise naturally in hydrodynamics: namely, the metrics induced on the space of dynamic free boundaries or on the space of vortex sheets by the kinetic energy of the surrounding incompressible fluid (where, for a normal velocity field $a$ on a hypersurface $\Gamma$, the squared norm is $\|a\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}^2 = \int_\Gamma a\, \mathcal{N}^{-1} a\, dS$ with $\mathcal{N}$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, or analogously a vortex-sheet kinetic-energy norm).

Develop the differential geometry of $(\mathcal{S}, g_{H^{-1/2}})$: in particular, determine the geodesic equation, the Levi-Civita connection, sectional curvature, completeness properties (metric and geodesic), existence of minimizing geodesics, the structure of the exponential map, and the relationship of these geodesics to the free-boundary Euler equations and to the Birkhoff–Rott vortex-sheet evolution.
artifact.status_search_result: No comprehensive treatment of the differential geometry of shape spaces equipped with the nonlocal $H^{-1/2}$ metrics arising from free-boundary/vortex-sheet hydrodynamics appears in the literature. Related work (e.g., vortex-sheet motion as groupoid Euler–Arnold geodesics for an $L^2$ metric, and Sobolev metrics of nonnegative order on shape spaces) is available, but the specific $H^{-1/2}$ shape-space geometry is posed as a research direction and seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Vortex sheets and diffeomorphism groupoids
status_evidence.snippet: The motion of vortex sheets admits a geodesic interpretation for a metric on the sheets; Euler equations with vortex sheet are groupoid Euler–Arnold equations for the L^2-metric.
status_evidence.claim: Related geometric framework for vortex sheets exists but uses L^2-type metrics, not a developed H^{-1/2} shape-space geometry.
